t: Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher: a plain-language overview
title: Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher does and why archives need it. A cross-archive identifier matcher links the same record across different archives: the book here and the book there share an ISBN, so they are one work. It normalizes identifiers, consults crosswalk tables, and connects records archive to archive. Separate catalogs become one web.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher works
title: How the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher works
description: Overview: what the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher does and why archives need it. Real matchers normalize identifiers (strip hyphens from ISBNs, uppercase DOI prefixes, trim whitespace), consult crosswalk tables mapping one scheme to another (ISBN↔OCLC, VIAF↔ISNI), and fall back to fuzzy title/author matching when no shared identifier exists. Each link carries its evidence chain — which identifiers matched, through which crosswalk — and conflicting links (one record matching two) go to review. The result is a same-as graph spanning archives.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher works: the deep tour
title: How the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Cross-Archive Identifier Matcher does and why archives need it. Real matchers normalize identifiers (strip hyphens from ISBNs, uppercase DOI prefixes, trim whitespace), consult crosswalk tables mapping one scheme to another (ISBN↔OCLC, VIAF↔ISNI), and fall back to fuzzy title/author matching when no shared identifier exists. Each link carries its evidence chain — which identifiers matched, through which crosswalk — and conflicting links (one record matching two) go to review. The result is a same-as graph spanning archives. Advanced matchers version their crosswalks, detect identifier collisions (one ISBN reused in error), and propagate links transitively with consistency checks. Quality is measured by link precision/recall on gold-standard cross-archive pairs. The limits are archives with no shared identifiers and no reliable metadata — those links stay proposed-with-low-confidence rather than asserted, because a wrong same-as link merges two different works' histories.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
